Naming convention
Element	Format	Example
Prefix	2–4 uppercase letters, unique across all specs	TXT
Spec file	<prefix>-<feature-name>-spec.md	specs/TXT-transaction-types-spex.md
Spec title	# <PREFIX>: <Feature Name>	# TXT: Transaction Types
Requirement ID	<PREFIX>-<2-digit number>	TXT-03
Requirement heading	### <ID>: <Short title>	### TXT-03: Split transactions

Prefix is unique across all spec files.
Starting the file name with the prefix makes ls specs/ sort and read like an index. It also means you can find any ID's file just by its prefix.

Picking a prefix
Two-word names: use initials plus one more letter, or a recognizable abbreviation. Financial Summary → FS or FSUM; Transaction Types → TXT.
One-word names: use the first three consonants. Budgets → BDG; Accounts → ACC.
Make it pronounceable or obvious. If you'd have to look it up, pick another.
Check the registry first so it doesn't collide with an existing prefix.
Rules that keep it consistent over time
Never reuse or rename a prefix, even if the feature is renamed. Old commits still point to it.
Never renumber requirements. If one is deleted, mark it ~~TXT-04~~ Removed: <reason> and keep going from TXT-05. If you split a requirement later, add new IDs; don't use TXT-03a.
Keep a registry. One file, specs/README.md, maps every prefix to its spec:
markdown
| Prefix | Spec | Status | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| FS  | [Financial Summary](FS-financial-summary.md) | Draft | Van |
| TXT | [Transaction Types](TXT-transaction-types.md) | Approved | Van |
